props.title: Live music for your engagement party.
props.lede: Two sets of parents are meeting over dinner, somebody raises a glass to the couple, and the song they’ll dance to at the wedding gets its first hearing. An engagement party is smaller and looser than the wedding will be, and the music is a jazz duo or a Spanish guitarist under the dinner, a singer who learns the couple’s song, and a trio if the party ends on a floor.

rows.text: A long table at home, at a Denver club or in a private dining space, the parents meeting the parents, a toast from each side, and the duo playing the standards under all of it.

rows.term: The cocktail party on a patio
rows.text: The summer version, with friends of both invited and the party the point more than the meal. A singer with a guitar or a duo plays it while the light lasts, the way a backyard party does.

props.title: Engagement party entertainment ideas.
props.lede: An engagement party is usually a dinner or a cocktail party for forty, so most start with the duo, and the rest follows from whether the night ends on a floor.

rows.term: A jazz duo the two families can talk over
rows.text: Upright bass and guitar playing the standards quietly enough that parents who’ve just met can hear each other, at home, on a patio or in a private dining space. The jazz duo is the same size that plays a wedding cocktail hour.
The song they’ll dance to at the wedding, sung once in front of both families by Tejas Singh, who learns it for the night and takes requests from both sides of the table for the rest of the evening.
A guitar with real technique in it under a long table, which is the first clip above, and the same sound couples book for the ceremony. Dirty Flamenco plays it as one guitarist or as a trio.

rows.text: When the friends throw it, it’s a party with a floor. Tony Medina plays it up to a four piece, and the DJ is there for the friends who want the night to run past the band.

items.q: Can we hire a band for an engagement party?
items.a: Yes. Most engagement parties are a dinner or a cocktail party for forty, so a jazz duo, a Spanish guitarist or a singer with a guitar plays the evening, and a trio or a quartet plays the party the friends throw. It's one contract with one personal contact, booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

items.q: Can the same musicians play the engagement party and the wedding?
items.a: Yes, on one contract. The duo from the engagement party can play the cocktail hour, and the singer who learned the couple's song already has it for the first dance. Tell us both dates when you write.

Quiet enough for two families who've just met to hear each other across the table, and the musicians stop for each toast. An announcement microphone is ready for whichever parent stands up first. A trio at the friends' party plays dinner at that level and turns up once the floor opens.

items.q: Can the band play on a patio?
items.a: Yes, under cover, with a wall socket through the nearest window. A singer with a guitar takes about 6 by 4 feet on one circuit, a duo 8 by 6 and a trio 12 by 8, and once the sun goes down the loud part of a patio party moves indoors or to the DJ. A certificate of insurance and a W-9 come with the quote if you need them.
